title: Factory Order Terms — One Production Order per Released Contract
content:
**Clause.** A customer holds one order under Factory Production Orders for every released contract, so the number of orders a customer may hold is not capped by itself; it follows from the contracts. Each order builds exactly one contract, a Window Replacement Contracts contract or an Entry & Patio Door Contracts contract, never both. A contract that already has a factory order that is not cancelled never gets a second one. Units remade for any cause stay on the original order.

## How the clause is applied

| Question | Answer under the clause |
|---|---|
| Is there a limit on how many factory orders one customer may hold? | No limit of its own; the count follows from the customer's released contracts. |
| May one order build a window contract and a door contract together? | No. One order builds one contract only. |
| May a contract receive a second factory order? | Not while it has a factory order that is not cancelled. |
| Do remade units open a new order? | No. Units remade for any cause stay on the original order. |

## Evidence

Whether a contract already has a factory order is read from the company's factory order records — the window contract or door contract the order builds, and the order's status — before any order is entered. An order in any status other than cancelled (entered, on hold, in production, shipped, delivered or closed) counts as the contract's existing order; a cancelled order does not.

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A homeowner with one released window contract and one released door contract holds two factory orders, one for each contract.
- A window contract whose earlier factory order was cancelled may receive a new factory order; a window contract whose order is in production may not.
